clue.text: Liberties taken after the match?

parts.note: the match is a wedding, not a game, and the liberties are the privileges a spouse may claim once married

explanation.surface: Players or fans take liberties once a sporting fixture is over.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the sexual privileges traditionally held to belong to husband and wife after the marriage ceremony.

clue.text: Fish consume most of power in the bilge

parts.note: the cod is a common food fish

indicators.note: only most of the synonym is used, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: to consume food is to swallow it
P is the standard abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: A fish ends up swallowing a lot of the energy down in a ship's bilge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bilge' looks like the bottom of a ship, which suits the fish, but here it is slang for nonsense. 'most of' drops the last W of SWALLOW.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are informal British slang for rubbish talk or utter nonsense.

clue.text: Distinguished Tory he-man with malformation

indicators.note: a malformation is a misshapen form, so the letters are bent into a new shape

explanation.surface: A Conservative strongman is notable for some deformity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'malformation' rearranges TORY, HEMAN and W (for 'with') together.
explanation.definitionFit: Something worth naming or mentioning is notable, which is what distinguished means here.

clue.text: Freedom of Hard Right to infiltrate three universities

indicators.note: to infiltrate is to get inside, so the two letters slip in among the others

parts.note: U is the usual abbreviation for university, taken three times
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
the third U from the three universities

explanation.surface: A political right-wing faction worms its way into several campuses, limiting liberty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to infiltrate' puts H between the first two Us, and R likewise slips in before the third, giving U-H-U-R-U. 'Hard Right' looks like one political phrase but gives two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: This Swahili word for liberty became a rallying cry of Kenyan and East African independence movements.

clue.text: Turbine ran G-force wildly, producing thrust from this

indicators.note: running wildly suggests disorder, so the letters are thrown into a new arrangement

parts.note: G and F, with F the abbreviation for force

explanation.surface: An engine's turbine spun out of control under heavy acceleration, generating extra push.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wildly' rearranges TURBINE, RAN and GF; 'G-force' supplies G plus F for force.
explanation.definitionFit: In jet engines, extra fuel burnt in the exhaust behind the turbine gives a boost of thrust, so the process is what produces it.

clue.text: Reflective selection first to last

indicators.note: the word's end letter is brought round to stand first, so its letters cycle

parts.note: a selection is a choice

explanation.surface: Someone thoughtful about choosing, going from first to last option.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first to last' cycles the final E of CHOICE round to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Something echoic imitates or reflects sound back, like an echo.

clue.text: Successive Chinese leaders grabbing one for nothing in Thailand

parts.note: Chiang Kai-shek led China, and was succeeded on the mainland by Mao

indicators.note: one, the letter I, is taken in place of nothing, the letter O

parts.note: Mao Zedong followed Chiang Kai-shek as leader of China

explanation.surface: Chinese rulers in turn seize something for free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one for nothing' swaps the O of MAO for I (one), giving MAI.
explanation.definitionFit: Chiang Mai is the major city of northern Thailand, so the clue simply locates it.

clue.text: Pinochet's missile launch site

indicators.note: the apostrophe s reads as has: the name has the letters inside it

explanation.surface: The Chilean dictator's rocket base.
explanation.walkthrough: A missile here is a dart, not a rocket.
explanation.definitionFit: The oche is the line a darts player stands behind when throwing, the launch point for those small missiles.

clue.text: Reckon when caught out

annotationWithheld.why: Reckon when caught out (4), answer CAST: 'Reckon' defines it, but no parse of 'when caught out' gives CAST (AS and C leave a T unaccounted for), and no blog or database explains it

clue.text: Removes the assembly surrounding 'unt protests

indicators.note: the protests go round the outside of the clipped word

parts.note: demos are protest marches
taken as written, a clipped hunt

explanation.surface: Anti-hunting protesters take down a gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unt reads as a dropped-aitch 'hunt', so the surface pictures hunt protests.
explanation.definitionFit: To demount something is to take it down from its mounting, dismantling the assembled unit.

clue.text: See 1
Bluebeard's taking a breather; 'e's sired a failure

parts.note: a gill is the breathing organ of a fish

indicators.note: a failure is something gone wrong, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: The wife-killer pauses for breath, his fatherhood having come to nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failure' rearranges ESSIREDA into ESDERAIS. Gilles de Rais, the fifteenth-century French nobleman and murderer, is often named as a model for the Bluebeard tale.
explanation.definitionFit: This French marshal and notorious child-killer is commonly identified as the real figure behind the Bluebeard legend.

clue.text: Three times with mutual docking idea, I run wild search for us here!

parts.note: W is an abbreviation for with, taken three times

indicators.note: running wild suggests chaos, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A clue writer musing on a shared idea for docking ships runs wild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' rearranges MUTUALDOCKINGIDEAIRUN into the rest of the address. 'Us' is the newspaper itself, so this is its website at the time.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the web address of the newspaper's online edition, where readers could look for its content.

clue.text: London guild preceding the Queen Victoria Society

indicators.note: Victoria comes before the Queen in the assembled word

parts.note: Victoria is a major London railway station
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual crossword Queen

explanation.surface: A City livery company predates a royal society named for Queen Victoria.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen Victoria' looks like one person, but Victoria is a station and the Queen gives ER.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stationers' Company is one of the City of London's livery companies, the trade guild of printers and publishers.

clue.text: Speculator's a debtor accepting a bet

indicators.note: the debtor takes the bet inside it

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for debtor in accounting
a venture is a risky undertaking, a bet

explanation.surface: A gambler who owes money still takes on another wager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Speculator's' means 'Speculator is'.
explanation.definitionFit: An adventurer can mean one who seeks fortune by risky ventures, a speculator in business.

clue.text: Iberian poet banishing sickness from his island

indicators.note: banishing sends something away, so those letters are removed

parts.note: Mallorca is a Spanish island
mal is French for illness, as in mal de mer

explanation.surface: A Spanish poet rids his home island of disease.
explanation.walkthrough: Federico García Lorca was from Andalusia, not Mallorca, so the 'his' is only for the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Federico García Lorca was a celebrated twentieth-century Spanish poet and dramatist.

clue.text: Our base in Cyprus piped up a group of Greek ornaments

indicators.note: to pipe up is to speak, so the base's name is said and heard

parts.note: Akrotiri is a British sovereign base area on Cyprus

explanation.surface: Music piped up at a British base on Cyprus amid Greek decorations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piped up' signals a sound-alike. Akrotiri is an RAF station on Cyprus, where Britain keeps sovereign bases.
explanation.definitionFit: Acroteria are the plinths or statues set on the apex and corners of a classical pediment, the plural of acroterion.

clue.text: See 12
Hero cast in stone could be more of the same

definitions.text: could be more of the same

indicators.note: a casting reshapes material, so the letters are moulded into a new order

explanation.surface: A statue of a hero cast in stone could be repeated many times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' looks like sculpture talk but rearranges HERO and STONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Further examples of a thing, similar items, are what the phrase means.

clue.text: Man hiding shirt of a kind made of fibre

indicators.note: the island covers the letter, holding it inside

parts.note: the Isle of Man, so Man is an isle
a T-shirt is a kind of shirt, giving the letter T

explanation.surface: A man conceals a shirt woven from plant fibre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' looks like a person but is the Isle of Man, an island in the Irish Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Istle is a tough plant fibre from agave and yucca leaves, used for cord and brushes.

clue.text: Meddle with, fumble 'n' break it? Out!

indicators.note: to fumble is to handle clumsily, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: a clipped and, giving N
taken as written

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry at someone fiddling with something and breaking it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fumble' rearranges NBREAKIT into TINKERAB; OUT stays as written at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To tinker about with something is to fiddle with it in an unskilled way, to meddle.

clue.text: Mischief maker snatching Sapper's crest

indicators.note: the goddess grabs and holds the sappers inside her name

parts.note: Ate was the Greek goddess of mischief and folly
the Royal Engineers, RE, are known as sappers

explanation.surface: A troublemaker steals a soldier's badge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crest' looks like a badge or emblem; here it is a mountain ridge.
explanation.definitionFit: An arête is a sharp mountain ridge, a crest between two glacial valleys.

clue.text: See 12
Compiler of 8

definitions.meaning: The pseudonym of a crossword setter for this newspaper
the answer to 8 down means discarded or thrown off, as a snake does its skin

explanation.walkthrough: 8 down is CAST, which means the same as the answer in the sense of losing skin or leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a fellow setter's pen name; the other is a synonym of discard.

clue.text: Heroin freely available

indicators.note: freely suggests letters moving without restraint into a new order

explanation.surface: A hard drug is easily obtained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'freely' rearranges HEROIN; 'freely available' looks like one phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Something for hire can be rented, so it is available for use.

clue.text: Desert ship's master having punch-up in car

indicators.note: the fight takes place inside the car

parts.note: taken as written
a melee is a confused brawl

explanation.surface: A captain gets into a brawl inside a car.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'ship of the desert' is the camel, so its master is its driver.
explanation.definitionFit: A cameleer is a camel driver, and the camel is called the ship of the desert.

clue.text: Camera one's carried to Bear Island

indicators.note: the camera brand carries the letter inside it

parts.note: Kodak is a famous camera brand
one is the Roman numeral I; the 's means is

explanation.surface: A camera is taken along to an Arctic island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear Island' looks like the Norwegian Arctic island; it is an Alaskan island known for its bear.
explanation.definitionFit: Kodiak is an Alaskan island and gives its name to the huge brown bear found there.

clue.text: One appraises American bases thus: right?

parts.note: in American slang the asses are bottoms, bases to sit on
so means thus

explanation.surface: Someone checking US military installations asks whether they are correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bases' looks military; it is the American word for backsides.
explanation.definitionFit: An assessor evaluates things, such as property for tax, so this person appraises.
